note: Plain-English object names for the headline in BUILD-SPEC-v2.md §10. The collection record has no vernacular-name field, so these are authored. NOT CURATOR-REVIEWED - every entry needs sign-off before publication. `source` records where each name came from and is the thing a reviewer should check: `catalogue` means the word appears in the Museum's own brief_desc for that record and we are quoting them; `common` means a well-established English name we supplied for the species, and is where errors will be; `descriptor` means no vernacular name exists and this is a plain phrase drawn from the catalogue's own wording; absent means nothing defensible exists, and the UI falls back to the scientific name rather than inventing one. Many catalogue binomials are superseded, so a `common` name is the common name of the CURRENTLY ACCEPTED species - which is a claim about identification, not just about language, and is exactly what a curator should challenge.

Most are nudibranchs and anemones where the catalogue's only vernacular word is the group name itself, which would print the same phrase eight or nine times on one page and tell a visitor nothing. These are the first entries a curator could improve.
